p: Coal Road sits in east Leeds, near Seacroft and Whinmoor, and it's well placed for the A64 and the outer ring road. That means some of Yorkshire's grandest days out are only a short drive away.

Lotherton Hall, near Aberford, is an Edwardian country house with gardens and a bird garden that's home to a wide range of species. Kids love it, and the parkland is great for a picnic. Harewood House, a little further north, is a huge stately home with grounds designed by Capability Brown, an adventure playground and a bird garden of its own, plus seasonal events throughout the year.
In the city, the Thackray Museum of Medicine, near St James's Hospital, is a fascinating and sometimes gruesome look at the history of health, with hands-on galleries that children enjoy.

For a treat in the centre, the Victoria Quarter is a stunning set of Victorian arcades with mosaic floors and glass roofs, and the Leeds Corn Exchange, a round Victorian building with a dramatic domed roof, is now full of independent shops and cafés.
Back near Coal Road, the area has supermarkets and fast food outlets nearby, so it's easy to refuel without heading into town.
With so much to choose from, east Leeds makes a great starting point for a weekend in West Yorkshire, especially if you've got a mix of ages who all want something different.
If you're coming from York or the coast, the A64 brings you almost to the door, which makes this branch an easy stop on the way into or out of the city.
